title: Quentin and the Ember
premise: Freya Whitlock has spent her life in the Ember Valley, the one place in the kingdom where magic cannot follow, serving as a royal food-taster who builds immunity to poison one dish at a time. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands and names her heir to a country that was erased from history two centuries ago, Freya discovers the valley's magic-dead peace is a prison built on a lie — and that the crown has been hunting the map for generations. Pursued by the king's justiciar and shadowed by Quentin, a disgraced knight sworn to protect her whether she wants it or not, she must find the door out of the vanished country before the solstice, when the last of its magic dies and takes the valley's protection with it. In the end Freya chooses truth over loyalty to the crown, reopens the door, and restores the lost country at the cost of her own place in the only home she has ever known.
about_author: Astrid Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border treaties and disused maps before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in the machinery of old lies, and lives somewhere deliberately off the map.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet her in the royal kitchens of Emberhold, swallowing a laced broth and cataloguing the numbness it leaves. She is valued, contained, and quietly resentful of a life measured in sips. Emotional beat: restless competence — a woman expertly surviving a life too small for her.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Millrace
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses near the millrace, presses a leather-wrapped map into her hands, and dies whispering that she is 'the last heir of Vael.' The justiciar's riders arrive within hours, asking questions no taster should be asked. Emotional beat: fear and vertigo as her small world reveals hidden teeth.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, closing with Quentin's. Fleeing with the map, she learns the valley's magic-dead borders are not natural but maintained — and that crossing them will expose her to a world of working enchantment. A disgraced knight, Quentin, intercepts her, bound by an old oath to guard the map's bearer. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; trust offered like a blade, hilt-first.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Every Map
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They travel through borderlands where villages pay tribute to a king who officially doesn't exist, and Freya reads the map's true script for the first time. Quentin confesses his disgrace: he once obeyed an order he should have refused. Emotional beat: growing intimacy through shared guilt; loyalty beginning to mean something chosen, not owed.

chapters.title: The Justiciar's Mercy
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The justiciar Corvane catches them and offers Quentin reinstatement in exchange for the map and the girl. Quentin refuses — and learns Corvane expected him to, that his disgrace was engineered to make him useful exactly this way. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed; Quentin realizes his whole fall was someone else's design.

chapters.title: Salt and Old Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In a drowned coastal archive, Freya uncovers the truth: Vael wasn't conquered, it was bargained away by its own heir, and every food-taster since has been a descendant kept drugged and docile in the valley. Her immunity was never a gift; it was a leash. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve — the personal becomes political.

chapters.title: The King Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the capital and find the 'king' is a figurehead sustained by the stolen magic of Vael; Corvane serves not the crown but the bargain itself. A botched infiltration costs them their guide and nearly Freya's life. Emotional beat: despair at the scale of the lie, and the first hint that the door out may require a sacrifice neither can name aloud.

chapters.title: Oath and Ash
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Cornered, Quentin must choose between the oath that defines him and the woman it binds him to — because the oath requires returning her to the valley, and the map requires leaving it forever. He breaks the oath formally, before witnesses, choosing Freya over the institution that made him. Emotional beat: liberation through ruin; loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the solstice threshold, Freya confronts Corvane and the bargain's living terms: the door opens only for an heir willing to give up the valley's protection — meaning her immunity, her safety, her past. She pays it, speaks Vael's true name, and the erased country floods back into the world. Emotional beat: climax — terror transfigured into sovereignty.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with Quentin beside her. Vael restored, Freya declines its throne, instead founding an order of tasters and truth-keepers who answer to no crown. The valley's people must now choose their own country without magic's shelter. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — justice outside the law, a home rebuilt rather than returned to, and a future tasted carefully, one dish at a time.
